newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Chinese premier arrives in Brazil to promote trade.
newsitem.headline: Chinese premier arrives in Brazil to promote trade.

text.p: Chinese Premier Li Peng arrived in Brazil Thursday on the second leg of a three-nation Latin America tour to promote trade and commerce.
Brazilian officials said the government hoped the four-day official visit would strengthen economic ties between Latin America's largest country and the booming Asian nations.

Li's tour of Brazil, which will take him and a 166-strong delegation to Brasilia, Sao Paulo and the Amazonian capital Manaus, comes almost one year after Brazil's President Fernando Henrique Cardoso travelled to Beijing.
It has also been preceded by a steady stream of visiting Chinese ministers, many discussing greater cooperation in agriculture.
Bi-lateral trade totalled $2.243 billion in 1995, sharply up from $1.286 billion the year before. Brazilian officials said they believed there was considerable room for improvement.

Li will be signing three accords in Brasilia: one on further satellite cooperation, another on the environment, and a third allowing Brazil to maintain its consulate in Hong Kong after the British colony is handed back to Beijing next July.
Li, who started his Latin America tour in Chile, will be travelling on to Venezuela after Brazil.
